title: Gear Restrictions
content: On this page Thrownets Gill, Draw & Seine Nets Akule Nets Drift Nets Lay Nets (Statewide) Lay Nets — Molokaʻi Traps Firearms & Spears Drones Explosives & Prohibited Methods Gear Restrictions Thrownets Minimum size: 2-inch stretched mesh. Possession of thrownets with mesh size less than 2 inches in or near the water where fish may be taken is unlawful. Unlawful to sell thrownets with mesh size less than 2 inches. Gill, Draw, Drag, Seine, or Other Nets Minimum mesh size for nets generally: 2-inch stretched mesh. Unlawful to leave any gill net unattended for any amount of time. Unlawful to leave any gill net in the water for a period of more than four hours in any 24-hour period. Fishers must complete a visual inspection of the entire net within two hours of deployment and release any threatened, endangered, prohibited, or unwanted species. Exceptions All persons may use hand nets or scoop nets of smaller mesh to take fish and other marine life for noncommercial purposes only, provided the net (including handle and other attachments) does not exceed three feet in any dimension. Licensed pond owners or operators may use nets of smaller mesh to take young mullet (pua) to stock their ponds. Commercial Marine licensees with a Bait License may use nets of smaller mesh to take ʻiao, Marquesan sardine, gold-spot herring, or any other species for which the Department declares an open season for use as bait. All persons may use nets of smaller mesh to take shrimp (ʻōpae), ʻōpelu, and makiawa. All persons using surround nets with SCUBA may use nets of not less than 1½ inches to bag and transport fish captured with legal gear to the shore or boat. See provisions relating to taking akule (halalū) and nehu, and provisions affecting particular areas. Akule Nets Unlawful for any person without a valid commercial marine license to take akule with any net that has less than 2¾” stretched mesh, except landing nets as indicated below. Unlawful for any person without a valid commercial marine license to take akule using the bag net fishing method. Unlawful for any commercial marine licensee to take akule while using: Lay net fishing method with net that has less than 2¾” stretched mesh Surround net fishing method with net that has less than 2½” stretched mesh Bag net fishing method with net that has less than 1½” stretched mesh Unlawful for any commercial marine licensee to keep akule in a bag net in the ocean for more than 3 days without notifying the department, explaining the reasons, and when the bag net will be removed. Immediate removal may be required if necessary to prevent waste of akule or alleviate public safety risk. Use of landing nets of any mesh size is permitted, provided the opening of the landing net is less than 4 feet in any dimension (excluding handle). Use of throw nets with mesh of two inches or greater is permitted. Drift Nets Possession or use of drift gill nets is prohibited in State waters. Lay Nets (Statewide) Dimensions Minimum mesh size: 2¾-inch stretched mesh Maximum net length: 125 feet Maximum net height: 7 feet Permits and Identification Unlawful to possess or use a lay net without first obtaining a lay net permit. Fee: Hawaiʻi residents — no charge; non-residents — $25; duplicate — $10 Nets must be tagged as specified, attached at each end of the float line and lead line (at least four attachment points per net); each tag must legibly display the permit number. Unlawful to falsely identify (tag) any lay net. Nets must be marked by surface buoys as specified; buoys shall legibly display the permit number, be marked with reflective tape, and be visible above the surface of the water; two buoys per net (one at each end of the float line). Fishing Rules Lay nets may not be used during the period from ½ hour after sunset to ½ hour before sunrise. Unlawful to fish with more than one lay net at a time. Unlawful to leave a lay net unattended for any amount of time. Lay nets must be inspected completely within 2 hours after the beginning of the set; all threatened, endangered, prohibited, or unwanted species must be released. Lay nets may not be used for more than 4 hours during any set. The same person may not set another lay net within 24 hours after the end of a set. Lay nets may not be used in water more than 25 feet deep, except that commercial marine licensees may use lay nets in water up to 80 feet deep. Unlawful to use a lay net within 250 feet of another lay net. Multi-panel lay nets are prohibited. Unlawful to retrieve a lay net in a manner that causes any stony coral to break from its attachment to the bottom or into smaller pieces; no stony coral may be brought to the surface in the net. Unlawful to discard, abandon, or leave any lay net (or portion thereof) in the water for longer than 4 hours. Lay nets may not be used in freshwater streams or stream mouths. Prohibited Areas for Lay Nets Unlawful to use lay nets within: 3 miles of the shoreline around the entire island of Maui Off Oʻahu: south shore from Kawaihoa Pt. to Keahi Pt.; Kailua Bay from Mōkapu Pt. to Wailea Pt.; Kāneʻohe Bay between the sampan and ship channels. Detailed maps available at DAR offices. Lay Nets — Molokaʻi Special Rules Maximum net length: 750 feet when set end-to-end; maximum height: 7 feet; minimum mesh: 2¾ inches stretched. Net users must first obtain a lay net permit from the department. Net users must attach at least 4 identification tags to each lay net as specified; at least one tag at each end of both the float and lead lines (minimum 4 attachment points per net). Nets must be marked with at least 2 surface buoys (one at each end); buoys must display the permit number, be marked with reflective tape, and be large enough to be visible to the naked eye from 1,320 feet. Lay nets may not be set for more than 12 hours during any one set. The same person may not set another lay net within 24 hours after ending the set. Lay nets may not be set within 1,320 feet of another lay net already set. Lay nets must be inspected at least twice along the entire length during the set; all unwanted, prohibited, threatened, or endangered species must be released. Traps Minimum mesh size: Netting: 2-inch stretched mesh Rigid material: 2 inches by 1 inch Entrance cones: no minimum mesh size Traps for shrimp and ʻopae: no minimum mesh size. Traps must be portable and not exceed 10 feet in length or 6 feet in height or width. Aquarium Purposes Any person with facilities for keeping live fish in reasonably good health may apply for an Aquarium Fish Permit to legally use fine mesh traps or nets (other than thrownets) for taking certain aquatic life. Noncommercial aquarium fish collectors are limited to a combined total of 5 fish or aquatic life specimens per person per day. Bullpen Traps Total length of a “bullpen” trap may not exceed 2,000 feet (including the length of the guide(s) and pen). Total soak time may not exceed 16 hours. Bullpen traps must be set more than 1,000 yards from shore, except on Molokaʻi where they may be set: Beyond 500 yards from shore west of Kaunakakai Wharf Beyond 200 yards from shore east of Kaunakakai Wharf Unlawful to discard or otherwise dispose of any fishing net, trap, or gear (or parts thereof) in the waters of the State. Firearms and Spears Fishing with spears is allowed for all fishes, but must follow minimum size requirements for spearing of certain species, closed seasons, and other restrictions. Unlawful to spear any crustacean (except introduced freshwater prawn), turtle, or aquatic mammal at any time. Unlawful to pursue, take, or kill any fish, crustacean, mollusk, turtle, or marine mammal with firearms, except tuna and billfish that have been gaffed. Drones (Unmanned Aerial Vehicles) Unlawful to possess or use any drone for the purpose of taking aquatic life except with a permit. Drones may be used for simple reconnaissance. Explosives, Electro-Fishing Devices, Chemicals, Poisons, and Intoxicants Unlawful to fish with, attempt with, or have in possession on or near the shore where fish can be taken. Permits may be issued for certain legitimate purposes.

title: Regulated Areas
content: Regulated Areas Hawaii’s waters are managed through several types of designated areas that restrict or modify standard fishing rules. Select an island below to see specific area rules. Statewide overview of regulated fishing areas Area Types Marine Life Conservation Districts (MLCDs) — The most restrictive designation. Taking marine life is generally prohibited; specific exceptions vary by district. Fisheries Management Areas (FMAs) — Allow most fishing but restrict certain gear types, species, or methods within defined boundaries. Fish Replenishment Areas (FRAs) — Closed to all fishing to allow fish populations to recover. Community-Based Subsistence Fishing Areas (CBSFAs) — Special rules developed with local communities to protect traditional subsistence fishing practices. Public Fishing Areas (PFAs) — Freshwater areas managed specifically for recreational angling; a Freshwater Game Fishing License is required. title: Licenses & Commercial Fishing
content: On this page Recreational Licenses Commercial Fishing Bottom Fishing (Deep 7) Longline Fishing Dealers Oʻahu Aquarium Fishing Special Activity Permits Licenses & Commercial Fishing Recreational Fishing Licenses Nonresident Recreational Marine Fishing License Unlawful for any nonresident of the State who has attained the age of fifteen (except members of the U.S. armed forces on active duty in the State and their spouses and minor children) to fish for, take, or catch any marine life for noncommercial or recreational purposes without first obtaining this license. Duration Fee 1-day $20 7-day $40 Annual $70 Freshwater Game Fishing License Unlawful to fish for, catch, or take any freshwater game fish without first obtaining a Freshwater Game Fishing License. Angler Category Fee Residents over 15 years of age $5 Military personnel on active duty (and their spouse/dependents over 15) $5 Minors between 9 and 15 years of age $3 Senior citizens 65 years of age or over No charge Non-resident $25 7-day tourist $10 30-day tourist $20 Duplicate $1 Rules: Minors below 9 years of age may fish without a license when accompanied by a licensee. Where bag limits are specified, each licensee may take only one bag per day. The catch of a child below 9 years of age will be considered part of the catch of the licensed supervising adult. A child below 9 years of age who wishes to take a bag limit on his/her own must purchase a valid freshwater fishing license. Unlawful to sell introduced freshwater game fish. Commercial Fishing Commercial Marine License Individuals engaged in taking, selling, or offering for sale any marine life for commercial purposes (including charter fishing services) must obtain a Commercial Marine License. Fee: $100 (resident); $250 (non-resident); $10 (duplicate) “Commercial purpose” means the taking of marine life for profit or gain, or as a means of livelihood, when the marine life is taken in or outside of the State, and when the marine life is sold, offered for sale, landed, or transported for sale anywhere in the State. Every commercial marine licensee shall furnish to the Department of Land and Natural Resources a monthly report with respect to marine life taken and any bait used. Reports must be submitted no later than the tenth day of the month following the month in which the marine life was taken. Failure or refusal to submit a monthly catch report shall be cause for revocation of the license. Commercial Marine Vessel License The department will issue a commercial marine vessel license to any qualified individual upon receipt of a valid application and appropriate fee. A qualified individual must: Possess a valid commercial marine license Be at least eighteen years old Provide proof of identity Have no unmet child support obligations pursuant to HRS §189-2 Vessel Type Fee Vessel less than 22 feet, not used for longline fishing $100 Vessel 22 feet or greater, not used for longline fishing $200 Vessel used for longline fishing $1,500 Duplicate $10 Key rules: A commercial marine vessel license is valid from the date of issuance and expires on the expiration date of the licensee’s commercial marine license. A license is valid only for a specific vessel and is nontransferable. A qualified individual may obtain and possess more than one commercial marine vessel license at a time. Longline vessels: The commercial marine vessel licensee shall file an annual report with the department containing information about all crew members who worked aboard the longline vessel during the license period (identity, nationality, arrival date in Hawaiʻi, departure date, and any other information the department may require). This report must be submitted within thirty days of the end of the license period. Charter fishing vessels: The commercial marine vessel license satisfies the commercial marine license requirement for all crew members. It does not exempt charter fishing vessel passengers or customers from the nonresident recreational marine fishing license requirement. A “passenger” is any individual on board who is not a member of the vessel’s crew. If a vessel is lost, destroyed, stolen, sold, transferred, or otherwise no longer in the possession or control of the licensee, the licensee shall immediately notify the department and the license shall be terminated. The license shall be kept aboard the vessel at all times while participating in commercial fishing activities and shall be made available for inspection upon demand. Persons issued a commercial marine vessel license shall submit monthly reports of the vessel’s fishing activity. Persons taking bottomfish in the main Hawaiian Islands must also submit trip reports of their bottomfishing activity, in addition to monthly reports for other species. Bait License Commercial fishermen may apply for a license to take baitfish other than nehu for use in fishing operations where fish are caught and landed in the State. No baitfish caught may be sold or transferred except for bait purposes. Fee: $100; Duplicate: $10 A license for taking nehu may be issued to persons employed on live-bait tuna boats, only if the person’s principal means of livelihood is derived from tuna fishing and the sale of tuna, and the fish are caught and landed in the State; such nehu may not be sold to others. Each license shall cover the operation of one fishing vessel and must be carried aboard the boat at all times. Each licensee must furnish monthly baitfish catch reports to the Department of Land and Natural Resources. Commercial Uhu Fishing Permit Unlawful to take uhu for commercial purposes without a valid permit. Fee: $100 Annual Catch Limit (ACL) for commercial uhu fishery: 30,000 pounds The fishing season for uhu will close when the ACL is reached. Commercial Kala Fishing Permit Unlawful to take kala for commercial purposes without a valid permit. Fee: $100 Annual Catch Limit (ACL) for commercial kala fishery: 15,000 pounds The fishing season for kala will close when the ACL is reached. Bottom Fishing (“Deep 7”) Covered species: ʻulaʻula koaʻe (onaga), ʻulaʻula (ehu), kalekale, ʻōpakapaka, ʻūkīkiki (gindai), hāpuʻu, and lehi. Closed Season Unlawful to fish for, possess, or sell bottomfish species listed above during the announced closed season, except by permit. Gear Restrictions Unlawful to take bottomfish with any trap, trawl, bottomfish longline, or net. Unlawful to possess, while on board a vessel, both bottomfish and any trap, trawl, bottomfish longline, or net other than scoop net or Kona crab net. Scoop nets may be used to bring on board a vessel any bottomfish that has already been caught. Kona crab nets may be used to take Kona crabs. Trip Reporting Commercial fishers must report all “Deep 7” bottomfish catches within five days after the end of a trip. Minimum Size Onaga and ʻōpakapaka minimum size for sale: 1 pound. Non-Commercial Bag Limit Unlawful for any person without a current commercial marine license to take or possess more than a combined total of five bottomfish per day. Vessel Identification All vessels fishing for or possessing bottomfish must: Be registered with the department first. Display the bottomfish fishing vessel identification number: the HA number, NMFS federal fishing number, Coast Guard documentation number, or DAR-issued number, followed by the letters “BF” as a suffix. Letters must be no less than 6 inches high and 3 inches wide in black or contrasting solid color, placed on both sides of either the hull or the superstructure. The bottomfish fishing vessel identification number is valid from Sep 1 to Aug 31 and must be renewed annually. Longline Fishing Definition: Longline fishing is conducted with gear consisting of at least one mainline over one nautical mile in length, to which is attached a number of branchlines with baited hooks. The mainline is suspended below the surface by floatlines attached to surface floats. Unlawful to engage in longline fishing within state waters, or sell or offer for sale any marine life taken with longline fishing gear within state waters. Unlawful to possess, sell, or offer for sale any marine life taken by longline fishing gear that is prohibited by or in violation of rules adopted by the Western Pacific Fishery Management Council through NOAA. Dealers Kona Crab and Lobster Closed Season License During the closed season, a dealer may sell, or a hotel or other public eating establishment may serve, spiny lobster, slipper lobster, or Kona crab lawfully caught in the waters of the State during the open season. Fee: $100; Duplicate: $10 Special Marine Animal or Product Possession and Sale License Unlawful to possess, sell, or offer for sale any aquatic life or product thereof of any size taken outside the waters of the State, when the taking, possession, or sale of the same species is restricted if taken within State waters, without first obtaining this license. Fee: $100; Duplicate: $10 Oʻahu Aquarium Fishing Unlawful, within three nautical miles of the Oʻahu shoreline, while possessing a small mesh net authorized under a commercial or recreational aquarium fish permit: Possess a small mesh net more than 30 feet long or six feet high, or join more than two such nets together for a combined length of more than 60 feet. Take or possess any ornate butterflyfish, oval butterflyfish, or reticulated butterflyfish. Unlawful, within three nautical miles of the Oʻahu shoreline, while possessing a small mesh net authorized under a commercial aquarium fish permit: Possess a small mesh net and take or possess a daily bag limit of more than: 100 yellow tang, 75 kole, 50 Potter’s angel, 50 naso tang, 25 Moorish idol, or 10 Achilles tang Six of any of the following: yellow tang less than 1½ inches in length, yellow tang more than 5 inches in length, kole more than 5 inches in length, cleaner wrasse of any size Two bandit (banded) angelfish more than 5½ inches in length Operate a vessel with more than the above daily bag limits for the number of permittees on board, or more than three times the number of any bag limit, regardless of the number of permittees on board. Note: Commercial aquarium collection is prohibited pending compliance with HRS Chapter 343 environmental review. Special Activities Scientific, Educational, or Propagation Purposes Any person with a bona fide scientific, educational, or propagation purpose may apply in writing to obtain a Special Activity Permit to legally take certain aquatic life, use certain gear, and gain entrance into certain areas otherwise prohibited.

title: Other Management Areas
content: Other Management Areas These areas fall under the jurisdiction of DLNR divisions other than DAR, or other governmental agencies. ʻĀhihi-Kīnaʻu Natural Area Reserve — Maui ʻĀhihi-Kīnaʻu Natural Area Reserve Location: ʻĀhihi-Kīnau shore waters include the waters seaward of Cape Kīnau at a distance of 2,000 to 3,000 feet. Prohibited Remove, injure, or kill any form of plant or animal (no fishing). Introduce any form of plant or animal life. Operate, anchor, or moor any motorized vessel. See also HAR 13-209 (DOFAW) and 13-244-32 (DOBOR). Paikō Lagoon Wildlife Sanctuary — Oʻahu Paikō Lagoon Wildlife Sanctuary Location: Includes all State-owned land areas adjacent to Paikō Lagoon, and water areas within Paikō Lagoon. Prohibited Remove, disturb, injure, kill, or possess any form of plant or wildlife (no fishing). Introduce any form of plant or wildlife. See also HAR 13-125 (DOFAW). Kahoʻolawe Island Reserve Kahoʻolawe Island Reserve — 2 nautical mile perimeter; entry prohibited without KIRC authorization Location: The island of Kahoʻolawe and surrounding waters seaward to a distance of two nautical miles. DANGER: The Reserve is a former military range, and unexploded ordnance is present on the island and in surrounding waters. Permitted Cultural, spiritual, subsistence, preservation, restoration, educational, and fishing activities specifically authorized by the Kahoʻolawe Island Reserve Commission. Prohibited All entrance into and activities within the Kahoʻolawe Island Reserve, including all manner of boating, fishing, and diving, unless specifically authorized by the Commission. Contact the Kahoʻolawe Island Reserve Commission: 808-586-0761 (Oʻahu) or 808-243-5889 (Maui). Northwestern Hawaiian Islands Marine Refuge Northwestern Hawaiian Islands — Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument; entry requires a permit Location: Waters extending three miles seaward of any coastline from Nihoa Island to Kure Atoll, excluding Midway Atoll. Entry into the refuge is prohibited without a Papahānaumokuākea permit. Fishing or taking of marine life within the refuge is prohibited. Native Hawaiian traditional and customary practices are allowed with a permit. Other Restricted Areas (Other Agency Jurisdiction) Fishing and other activities may be restricted in additional areas under the jurisdiction of other DLNR divisions and other governmental agencies, including: Agency / Division Areas DLNR – DOFAW Alakaʻi Wilderness Preserve, Kauaʻi; Waikīkī restricted areas, Oʻahu; Kanahā Pond Wildlife Sanctuary, Maui; Waimanu Estuarine Sanctuary, Hawaiʻi; Hawaiʻi State Seabird Sanctuary (various statewide islands and islets); small boat harbor facilities DLNR – DOT Commercial harbor facilities U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service National Wildlife Refuge areas

title: Hawaiʻi Island — Regulated Areas
content: On this page Kealakekua Bay MLCD Old Kona Airport MLCD Waialea Bay MLCD Lapakahi MLCD Waiākea PFA (Hilo) Hilo Bay & Rivers West Hawaiʻi Regional FMA Puakō Bay FMA Kona Coast FMA Kiholo Bay FMA Kawaihae Harbor Kailua Bay FMA Keauhou Bay FMA South Kona Miloliʻi CBSFA Hawaiʻi Island — Regulated Fishing Areas Kealakekua Bay Marine Life Conservation District Kealakekua Bay MLCD — Subzone A (fully protected) and Subzone B (limited fishing) Location: Offshore of the Kealakekua Bay Historical State Park on the western coast of Hawaiʻi Island, from the high-water mark seaward to a line from Cook Point to Manini Beach Point. A line from Cook Point to the north end of Nāpōʻopoʻo Beach divides the District into Subzone A (north) and Subzone B (south). The Division of Boating and Ocean Recreation has also established provisions relating to boating, anchoring, and mooring within the MLCD. Permitted Within Subzone B only: fish for, take, or possess any finfish with hook-and-line and thrownet; any legal fishing device or method except traps may be used for taking akule, ʻopelu, and crustaceans. Possess in the water any knife, shark billy, bang stick, powerhead, or carbon dioxide injector. With a permit, engage in activities otherwise prohibited for scientific, propagation, or other purposes. Prohibited Fish for, take, or injure marine life (including eggs), except as indicated in “Permitted” above. Take or alter any sand, coral, or other geological feature or specimen. Engage or attempt to engage in fish feeding. Old Kona Airport Marine Life Conservation District Kealakekua Bay MLCD — Subzone A (fully protected) and Subzone B (limited fishing) Location: (1) Waters offshore of the Old Kona Airport to the Kailua Lighthouse, bounded by a straight line from Point “A” seaward 500 yards, to a straight line from the Kailua Lighthouse seaward 500 yards; and (2) a “No Boating Zone” within the MLCD bounded by a straight line from Keahuolū Point to the southwestern corner of private property at Point “B”. Permitted Fish for, take, possess, or remove akule by handline at night, and ʻōpelu by lift or ʻōpelu net method using bait or chum for commercial or home consumption. Fish for, take, possess, or remove any finfish for home consumption by throw net or pole-and-line (without reel) with bait from shore. Collect wana, wana halula, and hāʻukeʻuke with hand tool (no SCUBA gear) from June 1 to October 1. Use the state mooring not longer than three hours per boat each day on a first-come, first-served basis for non-commercial use. Commercial dive/tour operations may be conducted at the mooring and from shore with a permit. Prohibited Fish for, take, injure, kill, possess, or remove any marine life, including live sea shell, ʻopihi, live coral, algae, or limu, or their eggs, except as permitted above. Take or alter any sand, shell, coral, rock, or other geological feature or specimen; or possess in the water any device used for taking or altering marine life or geological features. Feed or introduce any food material, substance, or device as an attractant, directly to or in the vicinity of any aquatic organism (except for the purpose of catching and removing that organism as permitted). Anchor a watercraft in the MLCD, or operate a motorboat or other motor-powered watercraft within the “No Boating Zone” except for emergency or enforcement purposes. Conduct commercial dive/tour activities except as indicated in permitted activities above. Waialea Bay Marine Life Conservation District Kealakekua Bay MLCD — Subzone A (fully protected) and Subzone B (limited fishing) Location: Offshore of Waialea Bay along the northwestern coast of Hawaiʻi Island, from the high-water mark seaward to a line from Kānekanaka Point to the point immediately north of ʻŌhai Point. Permitted Have or possess any fishing pole and hook-and-line, and fish for, take, or possess any finfish using such gear. Possess in the water any knife, shark billy, bang stick, powerhead, or carbon dioxide injector. With a permit: possess and use legal nets to fish for, take, or possess finfishes over the sandy bottom areas within the District; also engage in activities otherwise prohibited for scientific, propagation, or other purposes. Prohibited Fish for, take, or injure any marine life (including eggs), or possess in the water any device used for taking marine life, except as indicated above. Take or alter any sand, coral, or other geological feature or specimen; or possess in the water any device used for taking or altering geological features. Engage or attempt to engage in fish feeding. Lapakahi Marine Life Conservation District Kealakekua Bay MLCD — Subzone A (fully protected) and Subzone B (limited fishing) Location: Encompasses Subzone A (Koaiʻe Cove) and Subzone B, the adjacent shoreline area extending approximately 500 feet offshore of the Lapakahi State Historical Park on the northwestern coast of Hawaiʻi Island. Permitted Within Subzone B only: fish for, take, or possess any ʻōpelu by lift or ʻōpelu net; any finfish or crustacean by hook-and-line or thrownet. Possess in the water any knife, shark billy, bang stick, powerhead, or carbon dioxide injector. With a permit, engage in activities otherwise prohibited for scientific, propagation, or other purposes. Prohibited Fish for, take, or injure any marine life (including eggs), or possess in the water any device used for taking marine life. Take or alter any sand, coral, or other geological feature or specimen; or possess in the water any device used for taking or altering geological features. Engage or attempt to engage in fish feeding. Waiākea Public Fishing Area Waiākea PFA — Wailoa River State Park, Hilo Location: That portion of the Waiākea fish pond in the Wailoa River State Park in Hilo, south of the footbridge over Wailoa River, including the flood control channel and Mahohuli fish pond. A boat launching ramp is located within the park. Rules of the State Parks System also apply. Permitted Fish with not more than one line and one lure, or two single hooks in tandem no more than two inches apart. Use a dip net not exceeding 18 inches in diameter to land crabs lured to baited lines or to catch shrimp for bait purposes. Fish for, take, or possess an overall total of 20 fishes that include āholehole, ulua (including pāpio), and mullet, provided mullet shall not comprise more than ten fishes. With a valid Freshwater Game Fishing License, fish for, take, or possess any introduced freshwater game fishes. Prohibited Operate boats for purposes other than fishing; use boats constructed of material other than wood unless provided with flotation; for any juvenile under 13 to operate any boat unless accompanied by an adult 18 or older; propel any boat with a fossil fuel motor; operate any boat between 7:30 pm and 6:30 am; or operate a boat at any time without a life preserver for each occupant. Permanently moor any boat. Swim, water ski, or engage in any other activity requiring immersion. Snag any fish. Enter into or fish in any area posted as fishing reserves or prohibited fishing zones. Fish for mullet during the closed season. Take or possess more than 3 Samoan crabs per day, or any Samoan crab less than 6 inches in width. Possess or use a spear. Hilo Bay, Wailoa River, and Wailuku River Hilo Bay, Wailoa River, and Wailuku River fishing restrictions Location: Hilo Harbor — That portion of the bay in Hilo bounded seaward by the breakwater, and a line from the tip of the breakwater southwestward to Āleʻaleʻa Point. Wailoa River — That part of Wailoa River bounded by a line drawn across the mouth of the river and the footbridge at the mouth of Waiākea Pond, including Waiolama Canal upstream to the highest wash of the tidal water. Wailuku River — That part of Wailuku River between the Māmalahoa Highway bridge and Wainaku Avenue bridge. Permitted Use of thrownets, ʻopae nets not exceeding three feet in any dimension, and nehu nets not longer than fifty feet to take nehu for family consumption or bait purposes. Taking of crabs with baited lines (a dip net may be used to land crabs lured to bait); or with not more than five crab nets not exceeding two feet in longest straight-line dimension and stretched mesh not less than two inches, provided nets are attended at all times. Commercial Marine licensees with a Bait License may take baitfishes. Licensed pond owners or operators may take young mullet (pua) or other small fish for stocking their fishpond (except in Wailoa River). Prohibited Take or possess any aquatic life in violation of a season, minimum size, or other law, except pua as noted above. Use nets, except as indicated in permitted activities above. Take or possess more than 20 fish of mullet, moi, and all species of ulua (including pāpio and ʻomilu); bag limit shall not include more than 15 moi or 10 mullet per day. Fish with more than two poles with one line each, or two handlines, or with more than two hooks or lures per line. Use traps. Spear any crab; take or possess any crab with external eggs, with missing or mutilated abdomen or tail, or with a puncture wound. Take or possess more than three Samoan crabs per day. Snag any fish. Use or possess a thrownet or spear in Wailoa River. West Hawaiʻi Regional Fishery Management Area West Hawaiʻi Regional FMA — extends from South Point to ʻŪpolu Point, including all MLCDs, FRAs, and NRAs along the Kona Coast Location: Extends along the west coast of Hawaiʻi Island from Ka Lae, Kaʻū (South Point) to ʻŪpolu Point, North Kohala, and from the high-water mark on shore seaward to the limit of the State’s management authority. Includes Fish Replenishment Areas (FRAs), Netting Restricted Areas (NRAs), Marine Reserve, and all Marine Life Conservation Districts and FMAs along the West Hawaiʻi shoreline. Permitted All types of fishing, except as prohibited below. Prohibited in Kaʻūpūlehu Marine Reserve Take any aquatic life, except the following may be taken seaward of the 20-fathom depth contour by hook-and-line: ʻōpakapaka, kalekale, lehi, gindai, onaga, ehu, hāpuʻupuʻu, uku, taʻape, roi, toau, nabeta, aku, ahi, tombo, aʻu, ono, and mahimahi; also Kona crab by Kona crab net. Possess any marine life except as indicated above. Possess or use any fishing gear other than hook-and-line and/or Kona crab net. Deploy any fishing gear shoreward of the 20-fathom depth contour. Prohibited in Selected Areas Fish feeding within any Fish Replenishment Area (FRA), Netting Restricted Area (NRA), Marine Reserve, or any other West Hawaiʻi Regional managed area. While within any FRA, MLCD, or FMA (other than Kiholo Bay FMA): Collect aquatic life for aquarium purposes. Possess aquarium collecting gear, or take or possess any aquatic life for aquarium purposes, except aboard a vessel in active transit (no collecting gear in the water during transit; boats adrift, anchored, or moored are not considered in transit). Lay Net Fishing Restrictions (FRAs and NRAs) Lay net fishing within the following FRAs and NRAs is prohibited: Puakō-ʻAnaehoʻomalu FRA, Kikaua Point-Mākoleʻa NRA (Kekaha Kai State Park), Nenue Point (Red Hill FRA)-Kealakekua Bay NRA, Hanamalo Point-Kānewaʻa Point NRA, Kanonohe-Kalīpoa NRA, Kaloko-Honokōhau FRA. Exception: Lay net fishing is allowed in Kaloko-Honokōhau FRA using a locally constructed, handmade lay net of natural fibers, in accordance with other lay net restrictions. Prohibited Within the West Hawaiʻi Regional FMA Take or possess any pākuʻikuʻi. Take, kill, possess, sell, or offer for sale any specimen of: Hawaiian stingray, broad stingray, pelagic stingray, spotted eagle ray, blacktip reef shark, gray reef shark, whitetip reef shark, tiger shark, whale shark, horned helmet, and Triton’s trumpet. Possess more than five yellow tang larger than 4.5 inches total length, or more than five yellow tang smaller than 2 inches total length. Engage in SCUBA spearfishing, possess both SCUBA gear and a spear at the same time, or possess SCUBA gear and any specimen of speared aquatic life at the same time. Possess aquarium collecting gear, or take or possess any specimen of aquatic life for aquarium purposes between sunset and sunrise; without a valid aquarium permit; or while on a vessel that does not conform to registration requirements. Possess or use any net or container underwater to capture or hold aquatic life alive for aquarium purposes, which is not labeled with the commercial marine license number(s) of the person(s) owning, possessing, or using the equipment. Lay Net Fishing (West Hawaiʻi FMA — General) Prohibited: Use of a lay net not marked by buoys as specified and legibly displaying the permit number of the person using the net. Use of a lay net within 1,200 feet of another lay net (except two joined nets). Use of a lay net in water more than 80 feet deep. Use of a lay net for more than four hours during one set; or to set another lay net within 24 hours. Leaving a lay net unattended (considered unattended if net or surface buoys are not within eyesight of the person using the net). Retrieval in a manner that causes coral breakage from its attachment or into smaller pieces. Failure to inspect entire net within two hours after beginning set. To discard or leave any lay net or portion thereof in the water longer than four hours. Falsely identifying a lay net. Lay net possession/use restrictions: No lay net without first obtaining a lay net permit. More than one lay net per person. Lay nets exceeding 125 feet in length or seven feet in stretched height; with stretched mesh less than 2-3/4 inches (three inches in Kailua Bay FMA); two or more nets joined for combined total length exceeding 250 feet. Multi-panel lay nets. A lay net without at least four identification tags as specified by DLNR (attached at each end of float and lead lines; permit number must be legibly displayed). Persons using a vessel or float may use a total maximum of 250 feet of lay net, provided that at least two people are present and associated with the same vessel or float. Aquarium Collecting Permits and Vessel Registration A West Hawaiʻi aquarium permit is required to engage in aquarium collecting activities. Holders of an aquarium permit may only take certain species; there are daily bag limits for achilles tang and certain sized kole. A copy of the “white list” and other restrictions may be obtained at the Kona DAR office or by downloading the administrative rule. All aquarium-fishing vessels shall: Be registered yearly with DLNR to take marine life for that purpose. Permanently display the letters “AQ” on both sides as specified by rule. Fly a stiffened flag or pennant with the letter “A” as specified. Display a dive flag when divers are in the water. In the event an aquarium collecting vessel becomes inoperable, the operator shall immediately notify DOCARE or the United States Coast Guard by VHF radio and/or cellular phone. Puakō Bay and Puakō Reef Fisheries Management Area Kealakekua Bay MLCD — Subzone A (fully protected) and Subzone B (limited fishing) Location: That portion of the reef from the shoreline at the westernmost edge of the boat ramp, along a line drawn parallel with the ramp seaward to the edge of the fringing reef north of Puakō Point, then southwesterly following the fringing reef a minimum seaward distance of 250 yards (or to the edge of the fringing reef if one occurs beyond 250 yards), to a line due west of the small cove at the southern end of Puakō Beach Road. Permitted Possess aboard any boat or watercraft any legal fishing gear and any fish or other aquatic life taken outside of the area. With a permit, engage in activities otherwise prohibited for scientific, propagation, or other purposes. Prohibited Possess or use any type of net except thrownet. Engage or attempt to engage in fish feeding. Kona Coast Fisheries Management Area Kona Coast FMA — four zones: Wawāloli, Papawai Bay, Kailua Bay, and Red Hill Location: Four FMA Zones on the southwestern portion of Hawaiʻi Island, each bounded by two lines extending seaward at right angles from shore and marked by signs on shore. The seaward boundary is at a depth of 100 fathoms (600 ft): (a) “Wawāloli Zone” — From south of Wawāloli Beach to south of Wāwahiwaʻa Point (b) “Papawai Bay Zone” — From Keahuolu Point to the northwestern end of the runway of the Old Kona Airport (c) “Kailua Bay Zone” — From Kukailimoku Point near the Kailua lighthouse to the former swimming pool at the Kona Inn Shopping Village (d) “Red Hill Zone” — From Puʻu Ōhau (“Red Hill”) to Onouli Permitted Catch fish in the Zones with legal fishing gear for personal consumption. Prohibited Collect any aquarium fish within the Zones. Engage in fish feeding within the Zones, except for ʻōpelu fishing. Kiholo Bay Fisheries Management Area Kiholo Bay FMA — includes Wainānāliʻi Pond (excludes Luahinewai Pond) Location: That part of Kiholo Bay enclosed by a straight line drawn from Nāwaikūlua Point to Hou Point, including the lagoon known as Wainānāliʻi Pond, but not Luahinewai Pond. Permitted Aquarium fish permittees may use small-meshed nets other than thrownets, provided the person is within visual range of the net at all times. Prohibited Possess gill nets within the Fisheries Management Area. Engage or attempt to engage in fish feeding. Kawaihae Harbor Kawaihae Harbor — Zone A and Zone B fishing rules Location: Kawaihae, South Kohala, on the northwest coast of Hawaiʻi Island. Restrictions apply to the south small boat basin. Permitted Take any legal-size fish in season with not more than two lines, or two poles or rods and lines. Use hand nets not exceeding three feet in any dimension to take shrimp or nehu for bait purposes, or to land fish already hooked. Within Zone B only: use nets of mesh size not less than 3 inches to take fish, or akule net to take akule only, provided nets shall not be in the water between sunset and sunrise, or remain in the water except during active retrieval or unloading of fish. Within Zone B only: use spears or thrownets. Commercial Marine licensees with a Bait License may take baitfishes. Licensed pond owners or operators may take young mullet (pua) or other small fish for stocking their fishpond. Prohibited Snag or attempt to snag any fish. Herd, chase, or paʻipaʻi fish out of Zone A by swimming, diving, or from a boat, resulting in fish being taken by net. Otherwise fish for or take aquatic life, except as indicated in permitted activities above. Engage or attempt to engage in fish feeding. Kailua Bay Fisheries Management Area Kealakekua Bay MLCD — Subzone A (fully protected) and Subzone B (limited fishing) Location: That portion of Kailua Bay enclosed by a straight line drawn from Kukailimoku Point to the seawall of the Royal Kona Resort. A line from the northern edge of the channel at “Thurston Point” to the corner (“Wīha Point”) south of Huliheʻe Palace and north of the former Kona Inn Hotel separates Zone A (northwestern portion) from the seaward Zone B. Permitted Take any legal-size fish in season with not more than two lines, or two rods and lines, and with not more than two hooks each. Take crabs with not more than 10 nets, provided nets are not more than two feet in diameter. Take shrimp for bait with a hand net, provided the net is not more than three feet in any dimension. Possess any spear or thrownet while transiting Zone A. Within Zone B only: use nets of mesh size not less than 3 inches to take fish, or akule net to take akule only; provided nets shall not be in the water between sunset and sunrise, or remain in the water except during active retrieval or unloading of fish from that net. Within Zone B only: use spears or thrownets. Commercial Marine licensees with a Bait License may take baitfishes. Licensed pond owners or operators may take young mullet (pua) or other small fish for stocking their fishpond. Prohibited Snag or attempt to snag any fish. Herd, chase, or paʻipaʻi fish out of Zone A by swimming, diving, or from a boat, resulting in fish being taken by net. Otherwise fish for or take aquatic life, except as indicated in permitted activities above. Engage or attempt to engage in fish feeding. Keauhou Bay Fisheries Management Area Kealakekua Bay MLCD — Subzone A (fully protected) and Subzone B (limited fishing) Location: That portion of the bay bounded by a straight line drawn from Haikuʻua Point to Kaukalaʻelaʻe Point. Permitted Take any legal-size fish in season with not more than two lines at the same time. Use hand nets not exceeding three feet in any dimension to take shrimp for bait purposes only, or to land fish already hooked. Use thrownets in the zone bounded by a straight line from “Doc Hill” to the north end stairs in the wall fronting the volleyball court. Prohibited Snag or attempt to snag any fish. Use or possess nets, except as indicated in permitted activities above. Herd or chase any fish out of the area by swimming, diving, or using a boat. Engage or attempt to engage in fish feeding. South Kona (Miloliʻi) South Kona — Kiʻilae-Kēōkea to Kapua-Kaulanamauna boundaries Location: Waters off the coast of South Kona between the Kiʻilae-Kēōkea boundary and the Kapua-Kaulanamauna boundary. Prohibited Fish for or take ʻōpelu with fish or animal bait, except with hook and line. Miloliʻi Community-Based Subsistence Fishing Area (CBSFA) Miloliʻi CBSFA — southwest Hawaiʻi Island, from Paʻakai Point to Kaunā Point Location: Waters and submerged lands from the shoreline to the 100-fathom depth contour on the southwest coast of Hawaiʻi Island, from Paʻakai Point at Kīpāhoehoe in the north to Kaunā Point in the south. Contains numerous sub-zones. GPS coordinates can be found on the DAR website (administrative rules page, Part II, Chapter 60.10). Sub-Zones and Shoreline Boundaries Sub-Zone Boundaries ʻŌpelu Traditional Management Zone From Nāpōhakuloloa (“2-Stone”) in the north to Kākiʻo Point (Kaupō) in the south Puʻuhonua Pāpā From Lae o Kamimi in Pāpā Bay in the north to Makahiki Point in the south Pākuʻikuʻi Rest Area From Makahiki Point in the north to Kapulau (Honomalino Point) in the south Puakaiʻa Miloliʻi From Kapukawaʻaiki (Miloliʻi Lighthouse) in the north to Lae Loa in the south Puʻuhonua Honomalino From Kapulau (Honomalino Point) in the north to Pūkeʻokeʻo (Pōhaku Keʻokeʻo) in the south Puʻuhonua Kapuʻa From Kalapili (Okoe Bay) in the north to Kākiʻo Point (Kaupō) in the south Puʻuhonua Manukā From Kamoi Point (north point of Manukā Bay) in the north to the south point of Manukā Bay Permitted Possess prohibited gear and restricted species while onboard a vessel in active transit, provided no prohibited gear is in the water. Fish outside the four Puʻuhonua except as indicated in prohibited activities below. Within the four Puʻuhonua: Fish from shore using throw net, scoop net, and hook-and-line Fish from a vessel using hook-and-line Fish using a pole spear Fish for akule using legal nets Prohibited (Statewide) Aquarium fishing. Take or possess female ʻaʻama crab with eggs. Take or possess kole during March through June. From July through February: bag limit 20 per person per day, minimum size 5 inches. Take or possess ʻopihi kōʻele. Take or possess more ʻopihi makaiauli and ʻopihi ʻālinalina (with shell) than can fit in a one-gallon size bag per person per day. Take or possess pākuʻikuʻi before July 1, 2027. Beginning July 1, 2027: bag limit 5 per person per day, minimum size 5 inches. Spear uhu at night using any gear type. Take or possess uhu ʻeleʻele or uhu uliuli. Take or possess uhu ʻahuʻula or uhu pālukaluka during March through May. From June through February: minimum size 14 inches, maximum size 20 inches, bag limit 1 fish per person per day. Take or possess more than three other uhu per person per day; only one may be a terminal-phase uhu. Take or possess more than two ula per person per day. Take or possess any ʻūʻū from April through June. Prohibited Within Selected Areas ʻŌpelu Traditional Management Zone: Take any ʻōpelu except by hook-and-line from February through August. The four Puʻuhonua: Harvest any ʻopihi. Fish using any gear or method other than indicated in “Permitted” above. Pākuʻikuʻi Rest Area: Take or possess any pākuʻikuʻi. Puakaiʻa Miloliʻi: Use or possess any spear except pole spear. Spear any uhu, pākuʻikuʻi, weke ʻula, moano kea, or ʻūʻū. Use a lay net at night. Scientific Names of Regulated Species Hawaiian Name Scientific Name ʻAʻama crab Grapsus tenuicrustatus ʻOpihi ʻālinalina Cellana sandwicensis ʻOpihi kōʻele C. talcosa ʻOpihi makaiauli C. exarata ʻŪʻū genus Myripristis

title: Kauaʻi — Regulated Areas
content: On this page Hanamāʻulu Bay & Ahukini Pier Nāwiliwili Harbor & Port Allen Kapaʻa & Waikaʻea Canals Waimea Bay & Pier Kōkeʻe Public Fishing Area Wailua Reservoir PFA Hāʻena CBSFA Kauaʻi — Regulated Fishing Areas Hanamāʻulu Bay and Ahukini Recreational Pier Hanamāʻulu Bay FMA and Ahukini Recreational Pier area Location: The regulated region of the Hanamāʻulu Bay Fisheries Management Area is that portion of the bay, from the high-water mark seaward, bounded by a straight line from the tip of the breakwater westward to point “A.” The Ahukini Recreational Pier is a public fishing pier and a facility of the Division of State Parks (State Park rules also apply). Prohibited Swim in Zone 1. Use any draw, drag, seine, or other type of net except thrownet, crab net, or landing net not more than 3 feet in any dimension (excluding handle) in Zone 1. Take or possess more than 75 akule or more than 5 mullet per person per day in Zone 1. Use any thrownet or spear within 50 yards of the Ahukini recreational pier, or from the adjoining pier frame. Snag any fish or possess any thrownet while on the Ahukini recreational pier. Nāwiliwili Harbor and Port Allen Nāwiliwili Harbor Port Allen Location: Nāwiliwili Harbor — That portion of the harbor, from the high-water mark seaward, bounded by a straight line from the southernmost tip of the western pier northeast to the corner formed where pier 1 meets the eastern pier. Port Allen — That portion of Port Allen waters, from the high-water mark seaward, bounded by a straight line from the tip of the main breakwater northward to the bend in the breakwater of the small boat harbor. Prohibited Use any net, except a landing net not more than 3 feet in any dimension (excluding handle). Snag any fish. Take or possess more than 75 akule per person per day. Kapaʻa and Waikaʻea Canals Kapaʻa and Waikaʻea Canals — east Kauaʻi fishing area Location: Located in the city of Kapaʻa on the east coast of Kauaʻi. Permitted Take any legal-size fish in season with one line, or one rod and line, with no more than two hooks. Take crabs with not more than 10 nets, provided the nets are not more than two feet in diameter. Take shrimp for bait with a hand net, provided the net is not more than three feet in any dimension. Commercial Marine licensees with a Bait License may take baitfishes. Licensed pond owners or operators may take young mullet (pua) or other small fish for stocking their fishpond. Prohibited Fish for or take aquatic life, except as indicated in permitted activities above. Waimea Bay and Waimea Recreational Pier Waimea Recreational Pier — south Kauaʻi; pier-specific restrictions apply within 50 yards Location: Waimea Recreational Pier is a public fishing pier located in Waimea Bay on the southern coast of Kauaʻi, and is a facility of the Division of State Parks (State Park rules also apply). Prohibited Within 50 yards of the Waimea Recreational Pier: use any spear, trap, or any type of net except crab net. While on the Waimea Recreational Pier: Possess more than two fishing poles with one line each, or fish with more than two fishing lines, or leave any unattended fishing line in the water. Possess any thrownet. Reserve or occupy any space between the marks other than the one space personally occupied for fishing. Fish from any space between the marks already occupied by another fisherman. Kōkeʻe Public Fishing Area Kōkeʻe PFA — rainbow trout streams and restricted zones in Kōkeʻe State Park Location: Certain streams, reservoirs, and ditches in the Kōkeʻe State Park on Kauaʻi. Permitted During an open season announced by the Department on or about January 1 each year, and with a valid Freshwater Game Fishing License: fish for, possess, or remove rainbow trout with one pole and line, or one line using one baited hook attached to the single line. Fish only during the daily time period determined by the Department for that open season. Use a dip net up to two feet in longest axis (excluding handle) to land hooked trout. Take up to the maximum number of trout per licensee per day during the open season as determined by the Department for that season. All anglers must report before and after fishing activities at designated checking stations, and must allow inspection of any bag, container, vehicle, or conveyance used to carry or transport aquatic life. Prohibited Fish for, take, or possess any rainbow trout except as described in permitted activities above. Use any form of corn for bait. Use treble hooks or more than one hook. Possess spears, chemicals, trotlines, or nets (except as indicated in permitted activities above) or other illegal fishing gear. Enter into or fish in the prohibited fishing zone along a portion of Kōkeʻe Stream and its tributaries above Camp Sloggett, or any other area posted as a prohibited fishing zone. Damage or mutilate any private or public property, or contaminate or pollute any stream, ditch, spring, water hole, or reservoir. Operate any vehicle in any fishing area except on roads for vehicular use, or use any aircraft to gain access for fishing purposes. Wailua Reservoir Public Fishing Area Wailua Reservoir Public Fishing Area Location: Located off Kuamoʻo Road approximately five miles mauka of Kūhiʻō Hwy, above the city of Wailua on Kauaʻi. Permitted With a valid Freshwater Game Fishing License: fish using one pole and line, or one line with one lure or baited hook attached to the single line. Use a dip net up to two feet in longest axis (excluding handle) to land hooked fish. Take up to an aggregate total of three fish per licensee per day; fishers must allow inspection of any bag or container, or any vehicle or other conveyance used to carry or transport aquatic life. Fish only during the day (no night fishing). Prohibited Fish for, take, or possess any fish except as described in permitted activities above. Possess spears, chemicals, trotlines, or nets except as indicated in permitted activities above. Snag any fish. Possess or use any live animal or plant as bait. Enter into or fish from any irrigation infrastructure, including catwalks, valve towers, or ditches. Launch or use any vessel or floatable object (motorized, non-motorized, or wind-powered) on the reservoir. Swim, bathe, or conduct any activity in the reservoir other than fishing. Enter into or fish for any aquatic life at any portion of the reservoir designated as a wildlife or waterbird sanctuary. Contaminate or pollute the reservoir, ditch, or stream. Bag and Size Limits (Wailua Reservoir) | Species | Bag Limit | Size Limit | |———|———–|————| | Bluegill | 2 | 7 inches TL (minimum) | | Smallmouth bass | 2 | 9 inches TL (minimum) | | Largemouth bass | 2 | 9 inches TL (minimum), 14 inches TL (maximum) | | Tucunare | 2 | 12 inches TL (minimum), 15 inches TL (maximum) | Note: Bag limits are listed for individual species. The aggregate total bag limit of three fish applies. Hāʻena Community-Based Subsistence Fishing Area (CBSFA) Hāʻena Community-Based Subsistence Fishing Area Location: Waters and submerged lands from the shoreline to a distance of one mile off the northwestern coast of Kauaʻi, bounded by a straight line extending seaward at the boundary between Hāʻena State Park and Nā Pali State Park, and a straight line extending seaward at the boundary between Hāʻena and Wainiha. Permitted Pole spears 8 feet or less. Up to two fishing poles per person, with no more than two hooks per line. Throw nets. Paʻipaʻi net or surround gill net fishing methods, as long as nets are deployed from shore or from a vessel less than 14 feet long; two people must be within five feet of the net at all times while deployed. Scoop nets (may not be used at night, between 6:00 pm and 6:00 am); limit of three specimens of marine life per day with scoop net. Taking of limu by hand harvest only. Vessels with prohibited gear onboard may transit through the CBSFA as long as they remain outside the Vessel Transit Boundary. Prohibited Fish feeding. Taking of live shells. Taking of live or empty shells while using SCUBA. Spear guns. Spearing at night (between 6:00 pm and 6:00 am). Lay nets. Selling or offering for sale any marine life taken from within the area. Possession of prohibited fishing gear, except outside the Vessel Transit Boundary. Taking, altering, defacing, destroying, possessing, or removing any sand, coral, rock, or other geological feature or specimen. Bag Limits | Species | Limit | |———|——-| | ʻOpihi, pipipi, kūpeʻe, and pūpū | 20 total combined per day (from the ʻOpihi Management Area only) | | Lobster | 2 per day; hand harvest only | | Urchins | 5 per species per day | | Heʻe | 2 per day; may be taken only by hand harvest or with a stick no more than two feet in length | Regulated Areas Within the CBSFA ʻOpihi Management Area: Waters and submerged lands from the shoreline to a distance of 300 feet, from the Hāʻena/Nā Pali boundary of the CBSFA to a line extending seaward at the western edge of Keʻe Beach. Only place where ʻopihi, pipipi, kūpeʻe, and pūpū may be harvested, beginning December 1, 2017. Makua Puʻuhonua: Waters and submerged lands of Makua lagoon; a four-sided area bounded by: SW: 22°13’33.88” N, 159°33’42.41” W NW: 22°13’41.15” N, 159°33’44.67” W NE: 22°13’44.57” N, 159°33’34.71” W SE: 22°13’38.26” N, 159°33’31.56” W No entry without a special activity permit (applies to vessels and individuals). Vessel Transit Boundary: Waters and submerged lands bounded by a line drawn along the CBSFA boundary from the shoreline between Hāʻena State Park and Nā Pali State Park (Point “a”) at 22°12’42.50” N, 159°35’44.50” W to a point 1,000 feet offshore at 22°12’49.98” N, 159°35’51.79” W (VT1), eastward to a point 1,300 feet offshore at 22°13’35.57” N, 159°34’59.73” W (VT2), then to a point 2,300 feet offshore at 22°13’55.42” N, 159°33’42.00” W (VT3), then to a point 2,100 feet offshore at 22°13’48.84” N, 159°33’10.76” W (VT4), then along the CBSFA boundary to a point on the shoreline between Hāʻena and Wainiha (c) at 22°13’28.00” N, 159°33’13.50” W. This boundary does not affect general vessel operation or access to any area. Scientific Names of Regulated Species Common Name Scientific Name Kūpeʻe Nerita polita Lobster family Palinuridae or Scyllaridae ʻOpihi genus Cellana Pipipi Theodoxus neglectus, Nerita picea, Neripteron neglectum Pūpū order Gastropoda or Bivalvia Urchin class Echinoidea

title: Lānaʻi & Molokaʻi — Regulated Areas
content: On this page Lānaʻi Mānele-Hulopoʻe MLCD Mānele Harbor Molokaʻi Kaunakakai Harbor Lānaʻi & Molokaʻi — Regulated Fishing Areas LĀNAʻI Mānele-Hulopoʻe Marine Life Conservation District Mānele-Hulopoʻe MLCD — Subzone A (vessel-free) and Subzone B, southwestern Lānaʻi Location: Offshore of Palawai and Kamao on the southwestern coast of Lānaʻi. Subzone A — Bounded seaward by a line from Kaluakoʻi Point to Flat Rock, then to Puʻu Pehe Rock. Subzone B — Bounded seaward by a line from Puʻu Pehe Rock to Kalaeokahano Point. The Division of Boating and Ocean Recreation has established rules relating to boating, anchoring, and mooring within the MLCD. Permitted Fish for, take, or possess any finfish or ʻaʻama crab by pole-and-line from the shoreline only. Possess the following gear: pole and line; one knife; one hand net with frame no more than 3 feet in diameter (excluding handle); any legal fishing gear while on a vessel transiting to or from Mānele Boat Harbor within the harbor channel or the Harbor (but fishing gear may not be in the water). With a permit, engage in activities otherwise prohibited for scientific, propagation, or other purposes. Prohibited Fish for, take, or injure any marine life (including eggs), or possess any fishing gear, except as indicated in permitted activities above. Take or alter any sand, coral, or other geological feature or specimen. Operate, anchor, or moor any vessel within Subzone A. (Manually-propelled Hawaiian outrigger canoes may be operated, but not anchored or moored, in Subzone A.) Operate, anchor, or moor a vessel in such a way as to damage marine life or geological features anywhere in the MLCD. Mānele Harbor Mānele Harbor — Area 1 and Area 2 Location: Small boat harbor on the southern coast of Lānaʻi. Area 1 — Shoreline portion of the entrance channel and basin, bounded seaward by a line connecting the seaward tip of the three groins along the shoreline. Area 2 — Breakwater portion of the entrance channel. Permitted activities should not be construed as allowing activities otherwise prohibited by laws or rules of the Division of Boating and Ocean Recreation. Permitted Use and possess crab nets, hand nets for shrimp, and landing nets within Areas 1 and 2, provided the net’s frame is no more than 3 feet in diameter (excluding handle). Possess but not use nets on board vessels within Area 2. Commercial fishers with a Bait License may use and possess nets within Areas 1 and 2 to take baitfishes. Prohibited Use or possess any type of net within Areas 1 and 2, except as indicated in permitted activities above. MOLOKAʻI Kaunakakai Harbor Kaunakakai Harbor — Areas 1A, 1B, and 2 fishing rules Location: Southern coast of Molokaʻi. Area 1A and Area 1B — Portions of the commercial harbor, separated by a line extending from the Channel Range Lights. Area 2 — Portions of the small craft harbor. Permitted Within Area 1A: Fishing with thrownet or pole and line; taking baitfish in season with a bait license; fishing with nets with (a) a permit from the Board of Land and Natural Resources, (b) clearance from the Department of Transportation, and (c) except at night when nets may not be set nor remain in the water unless to complete unloading fish. Within Area 1B: Fishing with thrownet or pole and line. Within Area 2: Fishing with pole and line; using hand nets no longer than 3 feet in any dimension to take shrimp or land fish already hooked. Prohibited Within Area 1A: using nets except as described above; obstructing passage of vessels. Within Area 1B: using any type of net except thrownet. Within Area 2: using any type of net, except hand nets as described above.

title: Maui — Regulated Areas
content: On this page Molokini Shoal MLCD Honolua-Mokulēʻia Bay MLCD Kahului Harbor Kahekili Herbivore FMA Kīpahulu CBSFA Maui — Regulated Fishing Areas Molokini Shoal Marine Life Conservation District Molokini Shoal MLCD — Subzone A (crater, fully protected) and Subzone B (trolling permitted) Location: Offshore of Molokini Shoal, about three miles from the southwestern coast of Maui. Subzone A — Waters and submerged lands within the crater, bounded seaward by a straight line from the end of the submerged ridge extending off Lalilali Point to Paheʻe O Lono Point. Subzone B — Waters and submerged lands 100 yards seaward of Molokini Shoal and Subzone A. Permitted Take or possess finfish by trolling in Subzone B only. With a permit, engage in activities otherwise prohibited for scientific, propagation, or other purposes. With a permit, engage in commercial activities (excluding the taking of marine life). Prohibited Take marine life except as indicated in permitted activities above. Take or alter any sand, coral, or other geological feature or specimen; or possess in the water any device used for taking or altering geological features. Feed or deliberately introduce any food material, substance, or attractant directly to or in the vicinity of any aquatic organism by any means or for any purpose (except for trolling in Subzone B). Engage in commercial activity involving ocean users getting in or on the water (swimming, snorkeling, diving, kayaking, paddling, etc.) except as provided for by a permit. Anchor boats when a day use mooring system is established by the Department. Honolua-Mokulēʻia Bay Marine Life Conservation District Honolua-Mokulēʻia Bay Marine Life Conservation District Location: Along the northwestern coast of Maui, bounded seaward by a line from ʻAlaelae Point to Kalaepiha Point, then to the point at the northwestern corner of Honolua Bay. Permitted Possess aboard any boat or watercraft any legal fishing gear and fish or other aquatic life taken outside of the District. Possess in the water any knife, shark billy, bang stick, powerhead, or carbon dioxide injector. With a permit: bag and remove akule netted outside of the District, provided the net is moved only over the sandy bottom areas of the District; also engage in activities otherwise prohibited for scientific, propagation, or other purposes. Prohibited Fish for, take, or injure any marine life (including eggs), or possess in the water any device used for taking marine life, except as indicated in permitted activities above. Take or alter any sand, coral, or other geological feature or specimen; or possess in the water any device used for taking or altering geological features. Kahului Harbor Kahului Harbor Location: Primary port on the northern coast of Maui. The Fisheries Management Area is bounded seaward by a line between the seaward edges of the breakwaters. Permitted activities shall not be construed as allowing activities within any portion of the harbor otherwise prohibited by laws or rules of the Department of Transportation. Permitted Use a landing net with stretched mesh of 2 inches or greater to secure hooked or otherwise detained marine life. Use a hand net while on shore to take shrimp or other marine life, provided the diameter of the net is not more than 8 inches and the handle is not more than 14 inches long. Prohibited Use any net, except as indicated in permitted activities above. Take or possess a total of more than 50 marine life per person per day. Snag any marine life. Use more than two poles with one line and up to two hooks per pole (each hook having only one point); exception: double or treble hooks are allowed with lures. Take, attempt to take, or possess any marine life from the area, or use any fishing gear in the area that may otherwise be prohibited. Kahekili Herbivore Fisheries Management Area Kahekili Herbivore FMA — north Kāʻanapali; parrotfish, surgeonfish, and sea urchins protected Location: Off north Kāʻanapali. Northern boundary is a straight line extending 1,292 yards west from Honokōwai Beach Park; southern boundary is a straight line extending 335 yards west from Hanakaʻōʻō Beach; seaward boundary is a straight line connecting the seaward endpoints of the northern and southern boundaries. Permitted Fish for, injure, kill, possess, or remove any finfish or invertebrate, except prohibited species indicated below. Use bait or other attractants while fishing for permitted marine life. Prohibited Injure, kill, possess, or remove any rudderfish (nenue), parrotfish (uhu), or surgeonfish. Injure, kill, possess, or remove any sea urchin. Feed or deliberately introduce any attractant, directly to or in the vicinity of any marine life, except while fishing for permitted marine life. Kīpahulu Community-Based Subsistence Fishing Area (CBSFA) Kīpahulu CBSFA overview and subzones Kīpahulu CBSFA — southeast Maui coast with ʻOpihi Rest Area and Kukui Bay Sanctuary sub-zones Location: Southeast coast of Maui, from Kālepa Gulch in the west to Puaʻaluʻu Gulch in the east, from the shoreline out to approximately 60 meters depth. Contains two sub-zones. GPS coordinates can be found on the DAR website (administrative rules page, Part II, Chapter 60.11). Sub-Zones Sub-Zone Boundaries ʻOpihi Rest Area From Oheo Gulch to Kaʻū Bay Kukui Bay Sanctuary From Kukui Bay interior to Submarine Point to Puhilele Point Permitted With a permit, take akule while surround net fishing with SCUBA gear. With a permit, take introduced or invasive species of marine life. Transit through the area with prohibited gear or restricted species, provided no gear is in the water. Prohibited Take or possess: More than 10 finfish per person per day (akule and introduced or invasive fish not included) Any akule for commercial purposes More than 1 ʻōmilu per person per day More than 2 kala per person per day Any kole less than 5 inches in length Any moi from May–September; or during open season less than 11 inches or more than 18 inches long More than 40 ʻopihi of any species, or with a shell diameter of less than 1¼ inches or more than 2 inches Any ʻopihi within the ʻOpihi Rest Area, or while diving Any ula or ula pāpapa from May–September; or more than a combined total of 2 of both species per person per day More than 2 spotted reef crabs per person per day Any native limu species with holdfast (“roots”) attached Engage in surround net fishing, except for akule or taʻape. Take any marine life with a bag net. Possess a throw net with a stretched mesh less than 3 inches. Use more than two fishing poles; each pole may have only one line, each line no more than two hooks, and each hook only one point. Double or treble hooks allowed on lures. Take any marine life using SCUBA gear, or possess both SCUBA gear and marine life or fishing gear at the same time. Take or possess any marine life or fishing gear while diving from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise. Take or possess any marine life within the Kukui Bay Sanctuary.
